title: Observational prospective study to investigate the correlation of oral periodontopathogenic microorganisms with gynecological and senological neoplasms
summary:
Endometriosis, cervical cancer, and breast cancer are among the most common gynecological diseases. Many individuals affected by endometriosis suffer from chronic pain and numerous other symptoms. A widespread consequence of endometriosis is reduced fertility. On average, seven and a half years pass between the onset of symptoms and the diagnosis. For patients with an unfulfilled desire to have children, the delay is about three years, and for patients suffering from pain it can be up to ten years. Breast cancer is a malignant tumor of the breast tissue and is the most common cancer in women; approximately one in eight women will develop breast cancer during her lifetime. When detected early, breast cancer can be cured in many cases. Cervical cancer is the fourth most common malignant tumor in women worldwide and the seventh most common cancer overall. The average age at first diagnosis of cervical cancer has decreased by fourteen years over the past twenty-five years and is currently about fifty-two years.
Various studies have shown that the bacterium examined in this study, despite its natural presence in the oral cavity, also appears to promote tumor growth in other regions of the body and to complicate treatment. The aim of the investigation is to determine and compare the degree of similarity and the composition of the bacteria present in the oral cavity with those found in the three conditions listed above. The data obtained in the study are intended to help improve disease prognosis and thereby also contribute to improving treatment.
conditions: Endometriosis, Cervix Carcinoma, Mamma Carcinoma, Bacterial Oral Infection

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patient has signed the informed consent form to participate in the study.
- Initial diagnosis of a gynecological neoplasm or the presence of a previously treated neoplasm.
- atient agrees to and is able to comply with all study-related requirements (e.g., adherence to the required oral initial intake and participation in follow-up appointments and treatments).
Exclusion criteria:
- Immunosuppression (e.g., leukemia)
- Active systemic diseases (active systemic diseases such as tuberculosis, collagen diseases, multiple sclerosis, AIDS-related illnesses)
- Status post organ transplantation
- Severe internal medical conditions, e.g., severe decompensated organ disease of the heart, liver, or kidneys, or uncontrolled diabetes mellitus
- Pregnancy
- Inability to follow post-operative instructions
- Inability to attend the scheduled follow-up appointments
- Insufficient adherence to study-related requirements.
